fx_lock.source: European Central Bank reference rates via frankfurter.app

hourly_usd_all.ci_method: joint percentile bootstrap: each of 10000 iterations draws a divisor from the 21 hosts that publish their hours, reprices every retainer that publishes none, and then resamples the hosts. Seed 20260903.

us_monthly_native.ci_method: percentile bootstrap over hosts, 10000 iterations, seed 20260903

hours_sensitivity.basis: the published hourly headline, recomputed at each divisor. Only the retainers with no published hours of their own move.
hours_sensitivity.note: 12h was the median of the raw hours_included column before the audit, when hours per week and days per month were being read as hours per month. 52h is the median of every host whose text states a commitment once the v2.1.1 evidence scan is counted, and is the number the divisor would move to if the wider pool were adopted.

publish_rate.definition: hosts with a publishable rate for the role, over hosts whose captured pages mention that role

methodology.publication_gate: evidence and plausibility. The price, its currency and its cadence are found word for word in a quote captured from the provider's own page, and the price sits inside a per-unit plausibility band. Where the provider states how many hours the retainer buys, the divisor behind the USD-per-hour column is quoted too; on the rest it is the measured default of 32.5 hours a month, and no published record contradicts its own words. The word-for-word guarantee is a guarantee about the captured price, not about the derived hourly figure.
methodology.confidence_columns: strict_pass and dual_agreement are reported as a confidence tier per record (high = both, medium = one, low = neither). They no longer remove a row from the index.
methodology.value_basis: midpoint of a published range, labelled midpoint; a single figure is labelled published

normalisation.per_month: divided by the hours the provider publishes where it publishes them, otherwise by 32.5 hours per month
normalisation.hours_per_day_basis: 8. Corroborated on sackermanconsulting.com, which prices 4h as a half-day, 8h as a full day and 12h as a day and a half
normalisation.default_hours_source: host-level median of the 41 hours_included readings that survived the manual audit of all 51 (10 rejected: 3 SLA cells, 3 undefined 'units', 2 per-working-day intensities, 1 plan name, 1 bundled intern allowance)
normalisation.currency: converted at the locked ECB reference rate of 2026-09-03. Both the original currency and the USD-per-hour figure are published.

methodology.grouping: region is derived from the currency the provider quotes in, not from where the provider is. A country column derived from the ccTLD is published beside it and is empty for the ~90% of hosts on a .com.
methodology.dedup: one host contributes one value per group, the median of its own offers in that group
methodology.reporting_floor: a group is published only at n >= 8 hosts. Smaller groups are counted and named but carry no figure.

quality_flags.self_inclusion: saasfractionalcpo.com, the publisher of this index, is one of the sampled providers ($8,000/month at 25 hours; $15,000/month at 121.33 hours). It is one host out of 168, it is not excluded, and its median of $221.81 an hour sits at the 63rd percentile of the index.

groups_without_high_confidence.note: no record in this group had two independent extractions agree and the strict parse pass. The figures are published and counted; the table marks the group.

quality_flags.region_is_currency: regions US/UK/EU are currency buckets. A US provider quoting in euros lands in EU.
known_limitations: the hours default is measured on the 21 hosts whose published hours the manual audit accepted; providers that publish hours may not be typical of those that do not, and on this snapshot they are not: they are the more expensive tail
a monthly retainer is not literally a block of hours, so the hourly equivalent is a comparison device, not a quotable rate
the quartile spread of the hourly axis partly measures engagement size rather than price: across the offers that state both a price and their hours, hours rise almost in step with the retainer
ccTLD resolves a country for roughly one host in ten

hours_evidence.recall_note: v2.1 read hours only out of the collector's hours_included field and only where a manual audit had accepted the reading. v2.1.1 also reads a time commitment out of the offer's own price and cadence quotes, which recovered 20 further records whose published hourly figure had contradicted the provider's own words.
hours_evidence.open_question: the divisor in use is the median of the hosts the manual audit read. Across every host whose text states a commitment, including the ones the v2.1.1 scan recovered, the median is higher. Moving the divisor onto the wider pool restates the hourly headline and is a decision, not a repair, so this edition does not make it.

changes_vs_previous.why: method, not market. The snapshot is byte-identical to v2.1's; every difference below comes from three repairs: hours read out of the offer's own words instead of a default, a plausibility band enforced on the derived hourly axis as well as the captured one, and the publisher's own record corrected against its live page.
changes_vs_previous.note: figures for groups below the reporting floor are not listed here for the same reason they are not listed anywhere else.

published_group_withdrawn.reason: fell below the n>=8 reporting floor and is not published in this edition. The group is still counted and named in the groups file; it carries no figure.

changes_vs_previous.continuity_note: measured only on the groups that clear the reporting floor in both editions. A group of one or two hosts that did not move has not demonstrated continuity of a market; it has demonstrated that one provider did not edit a page.

quarantine.note: rows that clear the evidence rules and then fall outside a plausibility band. Named and counted here rather than dropped in silence.
